did_you_know.text: Did you know? This chapter says that the LORD incited David to count Israel and Judah—that is, to conduct a census of the people.
Did you know? David ordered Joab to go through all the tribes of Israel, “from Dan to Beersheba,” to count the people and determine their number.

Did you know? The census journey included the regions east of the Jordan, Gilead, the land of Tahtim-hodshi, Dan-jaan, Sidon, Tyre, and the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites, as far as the Negev of Judah.
Did you know? The census took nine months and twenty days, until Joab and the army commanders returned to Jerusalem.
Did you know? According to the number reported to David, Israel had 800,000 fighting men who could draw the sword, and Judah had 500,000 men.
Did you know? After the census, David’s heart condemned him, and he confessed to the LORD that he had sinned and acted foolishly.
Did you know? The prophet Gad presented David with three possible punishments: seven years of famine, three months of fleeing from his enemies, or three days of plague.
Did you know? In the plague, which killed people from Dan to Beersheba, 70,000 people died, according to the account in this chapter.
Did you know? David asked that the punishment fall on him and his family, rather than on the people, saying, “I am the one who has sinned… But these sheep—what have they done?”

Did you know? David refused to offer the LORD anything that had cost him nothing, so he bought the threshing floor and the oxen from Araunah for money. After he built an altar and offered sacrifices, the plague was stopped.
